observation_summary: SerializationUtils.clone() throws a ClassNotFoundException when attempting to clone primitive classes (e.g., int.class).
hypothesis: The custom ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream.resolveClass method fails to handle primitive classes because it only attempts to load them via Class.forName() using specific class loaders, failing to delegate to the superclass's resolveClass method which contains the necessary logic to resolve primitive types.
prediction: The fix will involve modifying the resolveClass method in ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream to include a fallback mechanism that calls super.resolveClass(desc) when the custom class loading attempts fail.
experiment_rationale: The bug report explicitly identifies that the custom override of resolveClass lacks the necessary fallback to the superclass implementation, which is required to handle primitive types correctly as per standard Java ObjectInputStream behavior.
reasoning_summary: The defect is in the procedural logic of the resolveClass method. It is an algorithmic failure to correctly resolve class names, specifically primitive types, due to an incomplete implementation of the resolution strategy. It is not a missing guard (Checking), a wrong value (Assignment), or a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object).
evidence_used: Bug report description identifying the lack of delegation to super.resolveClass
Stack trace showing ClassNotFoundException in SerializationUtils.clone

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves adding a check/fallback, the root cause is the incorrect implementation of the class resolution algorithm, not just a missing validation check.
